components.name: Button
components.example:
<Button label="Save" iconLeft="FloppyDisk" />
<Button label="Cancel" variant="stroke" />
<Button label="Delete" type="destructive" variant="ghost" size="sm" />
<Button icon="Gear" label="Settings" variant="ghost" />
components.whenToUse: Use the Button to trigger an action in the current context: submit a form, save, open a dialog, start a process, delete. The filled style is the primary action, and there is only one per view or dialog; stroke is the secondary action, lighter and ghost are supporting actions. destructive is reserved for actions that delete or cannot be undone.

components.name: Badge
components.example:
<Badge label="Paid" status="success" />
<Badge label="In review" status="warning" size="md" showIcon={false} />
components.whenToUse: Use the Badge to label a state or a category in one or two words, right next to what it qualifies: an order status in a table row, New beside an item of the Dropdown, Beta on a feature, the plan level in the account header. It is scanned in a list and read in a sentence; it is never clicked.

components.name: Alert
components.example: <Alert status="error" title="Payment failed" description="Your card was declined." actions={[{ label: 'Update card', onClick: retry }]} />
components.whenToUse: Use the Alert for feedback that concerns a page or a section and stays until the user acts or dismisses it: a failed payment, a saved draft, a plan about to expire, a step to complete. It sits in the content, at the top of the page or of the form, under the heading.

components.name: Banner
components.example: <Banner status="warning" title="Verify your email" description="Confirm your address before Friday." action={{ label: 'Resend email' }} onClose={dismiss} />
components.whenToUse: Use the Banner for a message that concerns the whole site or the whole account and that every page must show while the situation lasts: planned maintenance, an outage, a payment problem on the account, a policy change, a new version to adopt. It sits at the very top of the screen, above the header, over the full width.

components.name: Checkbox
components.example:
<CheckboxGroup label="Notifications">
  <Checkbox label="Email" defaultChecked />
  <Checkbox label="Push" description="Only for mentions" />
</CheckboxGroup>
components.whenToUse: Use the Checkbox when the user can select several options in a list, or to turn a single standalone option on or off, such as accepting the terms or receiving a newsletter. Each box is independent: ticking one never changes the others. The indeterminate state is only for a parent box whose children are partly selected, such as a “Select all” row.

components.name: Radio button
components.example:
<RadioGroup label="Delivery">
  <Radio name="delivery" label="Standard" defaultChecked />
  <Radio name="delivery" label="Express" />
</RadioGroup>
components.whenToUse: Use the Radio button when the user must pick exactly one option among a small set of visible choices, from 2 to 7. Showing every option at once helps to compare them, and preselecting a safe default means the group always carries a value.

components.name: Text input
components.example:
<Input label="Email" type="basic" icon="Envelope" required hint="We never share it." />
<Input label="Password" type="password" status="error" hint="At least 8 characters." />
components.whenToUse: Use the Input for short, single-line data the user knows and can type: a name, an email address, a phone number, a website, an amount, a search query, a password, or a link to copy. The type sets the right structure and keyboard: a country code for phone, an https:// prefix for website, a currency for amount, a magnifier and a shortcut for search, a show / hide button for password, a copy button for share-link.

components.name: Select
components.example: <Select label="Country" required options={[{ value: 'fr', label: 'France' }, { value: 'de', label: 'Germany' }]} onChange={setCountry} />

components.name: Dropdown
components.example:
<Dropdown>
  <DropdownItem label="Edit" leading="icon" icon="PencilSimple" />
  <DropdownItem label="Duplicate" leading="icon" icon="Copy" />
  <DropdownDivider />
  <DropdownItem label="Delete" leading="icon" icon="Trash" type="destructive" />
</Dropdown>
components.whenToUse: Use the Dropdown for a list of actions or commands opened from a Button or an icon button: more actions, account menu, sort by, bulk actions. Use the Select as a form field when the user picks one value among 6 to 15 options and the value is submitted with the form.
components.note: The panel is positioned by the caller (absolute under its trigger, left-aligned; flips when there is no room). Width 240 px; max 320 px.

components.name: Accordion

props.heading: ReactNode
props.grouped: boolean (set automatically inside AccordionBlock — pass grouped on each child)

components.example:
<AccordionBlock>
  <Accordion grouped heading="How do I cancel an order?" icon="Question" defaultOpen>Open the order and choose Cancel.</Accordion>
  <Accordion grouped heading="Payment methods" icon="CreditCard">Cards, PayPal and bank transfer.</Accordion>
</AccordionBlock>
components.whenToUse: Use the Accordion to shorten a long page when the user only needs some of its sections: FAQ, help pages, settings groups, product details, order summaries. The headings give the overview and the user opens what they need. Related sections stack in an Accordion block, 3 to 6 sections at a time.

components.name: Avatar
components.example:
<AvatarUser name="Camille Leroy" detail="Product designer" size="md" status="available" />
<AvatarGroup items={members} size="sm" />
components.whenToUse: Use the Avatar wherever a person must be recognised at a glance: comment author, assignee, member list, message header, account menu in the Dropdown. Prefer the photo; fall back on the initials when the name is known, and keep the icon for an unknown or anonymous person and for the placeholder before a photo is uploaded.

components.name: Breadcrumb

props.items: { label, href?, icon?, onClick? }[] (last = current page)

components.example: <Breadcrumb items={[{ label: 'Home', href: '/' }, { label: 'Settings', href: '/settings' }, { label: 'Billing' }]} />
components.whenToUse: Use the Breadcrumb on pages that sit at least two levels below the root of a hierarchy: a catalogue, a documentation, settings, a file tree. It sits under the header and above the page title, as a secondary navigation. It shows the path from the root to the page, not the history of the visit.

components.name: Tabs

props.items: { id, label, icon?: IconName | null, badge?, disabled? }[]
props.label: string (aria-label)

components.example: <Tabs items={[{ id: 'overview', label: 'Overview' }, { id: 'activity', label: 'Activity', badge: '3' }]} value={tab} onChange={setTab} />
components.note: First draft in Figma (page ↳ Tabs has no Documentation section yet). Render the matching panel yourself with role="tabpanel".

components.name: Header
components.example: <Header brand="RV Design" navigation={nav} navigationValue={page} onNavigate={go} avatarInitials="CL" userName="Camille Leroy" />
components.note: Mirrors the Figma `device` variable: html[data-device="mobile"] switches to the mobile composition (breakpoint 768 px decided with the designer; apply it in the app).
